The suspects, 26-year-old Alexia Goebel, and 22-year-old Mel Trez Coley, were both taken into custody. Inside the overturned vehicle, deputies recovered a loaded Beretta CX-4 Storm 9mm millimeter carbine, approximately 7.1 grams of fentanyl packaged for distribution, 159.5 grams of marijuana, loose plastic baggies, and a digital scale. and a digital scale. Goebel had her two-month-old infant in the vehicle throughout the incident. The child was transported to the hospital as a precaution and later released to a family member. No injuries were reported to the infant, Goebel or Coley. Goebel is charged with fleeing and eluding, child abuse without bodily harm, unlawful discharge of a firearm in public, possession of a firearm during the commission of a first-degree felony, trafficking fentanyl, possession of marijuana with intent to distribute, possession of drug paraphernalia, and knowingly driving with a suspended license. Her driver's license had been suspended since 23, and she has three prior convictions for driving while license suspended or revoked. Coley is charged with trafficking fentanyl, possession of marijuana with intent to distribute, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony, and possession of drug paraphernalia. He also has a prior conviction for robbery with a deadly weapon from 2021. Both suspects were medically evaluated, refused treatment, and were transported to the Escambia County Jail. Each was held without bond. As of 2026, both cases remain open in the Florida First Judicial Circuit.
